scenarios.hypothesis: A synthetic descriptor authorized in one queue generation is incorrectly accepted by the inert host backend after a controlled reset creates a neighboring generation.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled inert host counter records only the synthetic descriptor identifier and current queue generation; no real host resource or privileged action is touched.
scenarios.positive_control: The same synthetic descriptor before reset in its original queue generation is accepted by the mock backend and produces the expected inert receipt.
scenarios.negative_control: A neighboring synthetic descriptor with an invalid generation token is rejected by the mock backend before any bounded host-side marker can be emitted.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the experiment leaves the nested disposable guest-host fixture, reaches a real passthrough device, or requests any non-inert host capability.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After the fix, the stale pre-reset descriptor is rejected while a newly created descriptor in the current generation still produces the controlled inert receipt.
scenarios.guest_principal_boundary_intent: The synthetic guest principal is authorized only to submit descriptors to the owned virtual queue and has no authority over ambient host resources.
scenarios.interface_device_channel_identity: The owned virtual device, queue, backend attachment, and channel identifiers are frozen so acceptance can be attributed to one exact interface path.
scenarios.device_queue_channel_generation: The pre-reset and post-reset device and queue generations are recorded explicitly and differ by only the controlled reset transition under test.
scenarios.guest_controlled_object_identity: The test descriptor is a synthetic fixed-content object with a stable fixture identifier, creation generation, and no pointer to production host data.
scenarios.address_translation_generation: No real DMA is required; the mock translation generation is recorded so descriptor acceptance cannot be confused with an unrelated address remapping.
scenarios.shared_object_ownership_lifetime: The synthetic descriptor buffer remains fixture-owned and read-only, with lifetime extending through the comparison but no ambient host ownership transfer.
scenarios.host_consumer_identity: A single mock backend worker is the final consumer, and its process/thread fixture identity is recorded in the acceptance receipt for causal correlation.
scenarios.effective_host_capability: The backend can only increment an inert synthetic counter and emit a receipt, which bounds the observed capability far below arbitrary host execution.
scenarios.validation_ownership_decision: The decisive check is whether descriptor generation matches the current queue generation before the backend acquires any reference or emits its inert marker.
scenarios.lifecycle_transition_generation: The controlled device reset is the only lifecycle transition, and its before/after generation identifiers are captured alongside descriptor creation time.
scenarios.final_host_decision: The final host decision records accept or reject for the exact guest, descriptor, queue, and generation tuple without inferring any broader escape condition.
scenarios.bounded_host_result: The only accepted result is a reversible synthetic counter increment and receipt associated with this fixture, never access to real host files or devices.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: The receipt binds guest fixture, descriptor identifier, queue identity, queue generation, backend worker, decision, and synthetic counter value for this exact run.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Repeat the identical descriptor and guest principal with only the current queue generation changed; correct behavior predicts rejection of the stale-generation object.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Eliminate stale logs, retry semantics, backend restart, debug permissiveness, and descriptor-content differences by using one fixture and generation-only counterfactuals.
scenarios.evidence_level: GH3 — inert wrong-generation acceptance by the final mock host consumer is demonstrated without expanding into privileged or destructive host effects.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: GH4 — the case may rise only to a bounded reversible synthetic host marker; GH5 additionally requires remediation regression and complete lifecycle provenance.

scenarios.hypothesis: A synthetic shared page reference remains usable by the mock host consumer after controlled revocation, indicating stale ownership or lifetime authority across the boundary.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A read-only synthetic backend returns a controlled fixture label when the page reference is accepted; it cannot read production memory or mutate host state.
scenarios.positive_control: Before revocation, the same synthetic shared page is valid for the owned mock consumer and returns the expected read-only fixture label with a fresh receipt.
scenarios.negative_control: A never-authorized synthetic page identifier is rejected by the mock backend, proving the oracle is not merely reporting handler reachability or default success.
scenarios.stop_condition: Abort and do not proceed if the shared object maps production memory, another tenant, a real device buffer, or any host resource outside the nested owned fixture.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After remediation, the revoked reference is rejected while a separately authorized current-lifetime synthetic page remains readable through the inert backend.
scenarios.guest_principal_boundary_intent: The synthetic guest principal may share only designated fixture pages with the owned backend, and revocation is intended to terminate that delegated read capability.
scenarios.interface_device_channel_identity: The paravirtual shared-memory channel and mock backend endpoint are fixed to one owned fixture so reference lifetime cannot be confused across channels.
scenarios.device_queue_channel_generation: Channel and queue generations are recorded before and after revocation to distinguish stale shared-object authority from a legitimate recreated channel.
scenarios.guest_controlled_object_identity: The guest-controlled object is a synthetic shared-page handle with deterministic contents, explicit grant identifier, and no production data or credential material.
scenarios.address_translation_generation: The controlled mapping generation and grant translation identity are recorded before and after revocation so stale address translation can be separated from ownership.
scenarios.shared_object_ownership_lifetime: Ownership, reference holders, revocation state, and lifetime generation of the synthetic page are explicit and form the primary causal binding under test.
scenarios.host_consumer_identity: The final consumer is a read-only mock backend with a fixed fixture identity, and every accepted lookup emits a receipt tied to that consumer.
scenarios.effective_host_capability: The effective capability is limited to reading a synthetic fixture label from the authorized page abstraction; no host write, execution, or credential access exists.
scenarios.validation_ownership_decision: The decisive policy is whether the shared-page lifetime is current and not revoked before the backend resolves or retains the object reference.
scenarios.lifecycle_transition_generation: Controlled revocation advances the shared-object lifetime generation without changing the guest principal, page fixture contents, or host consumer identity.
scenarios.final_host_decision: The backend records a final accept/reject decision for the exact grant, lifetime generation, guest principal, and consumer tuple after the revocation boundary.
scenarios.bounded_host_result: A successful case yields only a read-only synthetic label and correlated receipt; it does not imply arbitrary memory access or guest-to-host code execution.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: The receipt records guest fixture, grant/page identifier, mapping generation, lifetime generation, backend identity, final decision, and returned synthetic label.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold the synthetic page and consumer constant while toggling only the authoritative revocation/lifetime generation; correct behavior rejects the stale reference.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Rule out stale receipt replay, cached fixture output, different mapping state, backend restart, and debug-only bypass before attributing acceptance to lifetime revocation failure.
scenarios.evidence_level: GH3 — inert read-only use of a revoked synthetic shared object is bound to the final consumer and exact lifetime generation without broader impact.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: GH4 — evidence is capped at a bounded read-only synthetic host result unless complete remediation regression and all GH5 provenance requirements are satisfied.

scenarios.hypothesis: The same guest-visible synthetic address is consumed under a stale memory-slot or IOMMU generation, causing the backend to bind it to the wrong controlled host object.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A mock translation layer resolves only synthetic object labels and the inert backend returns a controlled read-only identity receipt instead of touching real DMA or devices.
scenarios.positive_control: Under the current synthetic memory-slot and IOMMU generation, the guest-visible address resolves to the intended fixture object and the mock consumer accepts it.
scenarios.negative_control: A deliberately unmapped neighboring synthetic address is rejected before backend use, proving the controlled result depends on authoritative translation rather than handler entry.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop if validation would require real device passthrough, production DMA, host kernel memory, unrelated address spaces, or any mapping outside the owned nested fixture.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After remediation, stale-generation translation is rejected or refreshed while the current-generation address continues to resolve to the intended synthetic object.
scenarios.guest_principal_boundary_intent: The synthetic guest principal is authorized only to reference fixture addresses translated by the owned mock memory subsystem under the current generation.
scenarios.interface_device_channel_identity: The virtual device channel and mock backend are held constant so the experiment isolates translation generation rather than a different consumer path.
scenarios.device_queue_channel_generation: The device and queue generations remain fixed while only the memory-slot or IOMMU translation generation changes between positive and counterfactual runs.
scenarios.guest_controlled_object_identity: The guest-controlled input is one deterministic synthetic guest-visible address and request identifier whose bytes remain unchanged across the experiment.
scenarios.address_translation_generation: The authoritative memory-slot and IOMMU generations are explicit, with neighboring generations mapping the same guest-visible number to distinct synthetic object identities.
scenarios.shared_object_ownership_lifetime: Both synthetic target objects have explicit fixture ownership and stable lifetime during the test, preventing use-after-free from masquerading as translation confusion.
scenarios.host_consumer_identity: A single inert backend consumer performs the final translated lookup and emits its own fixture identity in the receipt for unambiguous attribution.
scenarios.effective_host_capability: The backend capability is restricted to returning the label of the resolved synthetic object, so the experiment cannot perform real DMA or privileged host mutation.
scenarios.validation_ownership_decision: The decisive check is whether translation is resolved from the current authoritative generation immediately before the backend consumes the synthetic request.
scenarios.lifecycle_transition_generation: A controlled memory-slot/IOMMU generation change is the sole lifecycle variable and is recorded before each otherwise identical request submission.
scenarios.final_host_decision: The host decision states which synthetic object identity was accepted for the exact guest-visible address and translation generation under the fixed consumer.
scenarios.bounded_host_result: The bounded result is a read-only synthetic object label plus receipt, sufficient to expose wrong-generation binding without accessing any production host data.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: The receipt binds guest principal, address, request identifier, device/queue generation, translation generation, resolved synthetic object, and backend decision.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Repeat the same request with only the translation generation changed; correct behavior must follow the current mapping rather than a stale cached host-object identity.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Eliminate stale translation-cache output, different device generation, fixture ownership changes, retry behavior, and unrelated backend activity before promoting the result.
scenarios.evidence_level: GH3 — a stale-generation synthetic translation is accepted by the final inert consumer and correlated to the exact address and mapping-generation tuple.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: GH4 — the case remains limited to a bounded read-only synthetic result until GH5 remediation regression and complete lifecycle/counterfactual evidence exist.

scenarios.hypothesis: A synthetic backend capability or host object reference survives migration or snapshot restore even though the restored device lifecycle generation should require revalidation.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A nested controlled backend exposes only an inert capability token and synthetic marker, allowing stale-capability detection without host execution or production resource access.
scenarios.positive_control: Before migration or snapshot restore, the authorized current-generation synthetic capability produces the expected inert marker and receipt in the owned fixture.
scenarios.negative_control: A synthetic capability from an unrelated fixture generation is rejected by the same backend, establishing that the controlled oracle can distinguish generation identity.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if migration or restore targets a production host, another tenant, real host filesystem, real credential, or any backend outside the owned nested environment.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After the fix, the pre-transition stale capability is rejected after restore while a capability reissued for the current lifecycle generation still succeeds inertly.
scenarios.guest_principal_boundary_intent: The synthetic guest principal is allowed only the documented mock-device capability and must not inherit stale ambient backend authority across lifecycle transitions.
scenarios.interface_device_channel_identity: The virtual device/channel identity is preserved in fixture metadata while backend and lifecycle generations are recorded separately across migration or restore.
scenarios.device_queue_channel_generation: Device and queue generation identifiers before and after the transition are captured so stale capability use cannot be mislabeled as normal current-generation access.
scenarios.guest_controlled_object_identity: The guest supplies one deterministic synthetic capability request referencing a fixture host object token with no connection to real host handles or credentials.
scenarios.address_translation_generation: Memory-slot/IOMMU translation generations are captured on both sides of the transition to rule out stale address mapping as an alternative cause of acceptance.
scenarios.shared_object_ownership_lifetime: The synthetic host object has explicit owner, lifetime generation, and revocation state so inherited references can be distinguished from deliberately reissued capability state.
scenarios.host_consumer_identity: The final consumer is an inert mock backend whose pre-transition and post-transition fixture generations are both included in the decision receipt.
scenarios.effective_host_capability: The only effective host capability is setting a reversible synthetic marker associated with the fixture token; arbitrary host execution or privilege escalation is impossible.
scenarios.validation_ownership_decision: The decisive policy requires revalidation of capability token, backend generation, object lifetime, and current device lifecycle generation after migration or restore.
scenarios.lifecycle_transition_generation: Migration or snapshot restore advances the controlled lifecycle generation and records source/destination backend identities without changing the guest request bytes.
scenarios.final_host_decision: The backend records acceptance or rejection of the exact pre-transition capability under the post-transition lifecycle generation and current ownership state.
scenarios.bounded_host_result: Acceptance produces only a reversible synthetic marker and correlated receipt, proving at most bounded stale-capability use rather than broad host compromise.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: The receipt binds guest fixture, capability token, device generation, backend generation, object lifetime, migration/restore generation, decision, and marker value.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Submit the identical synthetic capability before and after the lifecycle transition while holding all other variables stable; correct behavior revokes the stale generation.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Eliminate backend identity drift, restored fixture mismatch, stale logs, intended capability transfer policy, translation changes, and unrelated host activity before promotion.
scenarios.evidence_level: GH4 — a stale synthetic capability produces a bounded reversible host marker after the lifecycle transition with exact tuple and receipt correlation.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: GH4 — do not claim GH5 until remediation regression, complete lifecycle provenance, neighboring-generation controls, and alternative-explanation elimination are verified.
